Maya (AE): Heads-up — ZephyrCorp wants a 1-week POC to migrate off CompetitorX. They care about minimal client changes, predictable token billing, and a short security appendix. Can we scope owners?
Erik (SE): We should aim to present a drop-in facade for their existing client paths (/v1/generate, streaming) so client code stays nearly identical. Need sample client headers they depend on.
Samira (Solutions): I can draft a lightweight adapter that exposes /v1/generate and maps CompetitorX framing to our streaming chunks. Will also add a token-diff run against their 200-sample corpus.
Pri (Security): Security asks: EU-only residency, CMK/KMS support, redact-in-hosted-logs, IP allowlist, and a clause about not forwarding raw payloads during fallback. They want an answer in the vendor questionnaire by Thu.
Ola (Infra): Latency target: p99 < 240ms for short 32-token responses. Recommend dedicating a small eu-west pool for the POC. I can provision nodes if scope is locked today.
Erik (SE): Streaming detail: CompetitorX frames `{"event":"part","seq":N,"text":...}` and ends with `{"event":"finished"}`. Our runtime streams token deltas. Adapter should wrap our chunks into `part` events and emit `finished` on close. That will keep their client reassembly intact.
Samira (Solutions): Example shim snippet:```python
for chunk in read_stream():
  send_json({"event":"part","seq":i,"text":chunk})
on_close: send_json({"event":"finished"})
```
Samira (Solutions): For token billing: I'll run `tools/token_delta.py --a competitorx-v1 --b redwood-base --i zephyr_samples.jsonl --o zephyr_deltas.csv` and produce per-request deltas + aggregated monthly projection.
Pri (Security): For fallback: we'll provide a config flag to disable automatic fallback to third parties and an attestation: "No raw prompts or full responses are forwarded to third parties during automatic fallback; only routing metadata may be used." I'll supply exact wording.
Maya (AE): Legal also asked for a short note on rollback and data flow during failover.
Ola (Infra): Canary plan: 1) facade in staging (no traffic), 2) dedicated pool + smoke latency tests, 3) 5% canary traffic with immediate rollback triggers (latency/error/regression). I'll add trace tags to all POC requests.
Erik (SE): Tool mapping: CompetitorX uses `tool_response` object, we reply with `function_call` style. Adapter must map `tool_name`, `request_id`, and preserve content-type headers.
Samira (Solutions): Eval harness: 300 prompts, metrics = exact match, normalized edit distance, and embedding cosine. I'll containerize it so Zephyr can run locally against CompetitorX & our staging. Target: >=80% semantic similarity on core flows.
ci-bot: infra-provision: staging-zephyr created, 2 GPUs reserved, logs streaming enabled.
Maya (AE): Timeline: Zephyr wants a demo in 6 business days. Are we happy to commit?
Ola (Infra): Yes if scope limited to /v1/generate and the sample corpus arrives today. Need final scope by EOD.
Pri (Security): Questionnaire answers and attestation by Thu EOD.
Erik (SE): I'll prototype the streaming frame mapper and adapter today and push to the POC repo.
Samira (Solutions): Token-diff run queued; will publish CSV + README explaining tokenization edge cases (whitespace, separators).
Maya (AE): I'll send Zephyr a proposed scope doc and schedule a 20-min kickoff tomorrow. Thanks team :rocket:
